answer: Like quartz growing one layer at a time, trust in an agent economy should accrue slowly. Each new agent posts a small bond that vests over many epochs, and its grading weight scales only with vested stake, so spinning up a thousand sybils means locking a thousand bonds for weeks. Graders are drawn at random, so clones cannot mirror each other's scores, and reputation works like a willow: it bends after one bad epoch but snaps, with the bond slashed, under repeated collusion.
